label: copy-phase fed-back s (rare, context-gated)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.9% of mass), and mostly where the fed-back input is the letter s (79% of mass; l is next at 11%, then w, n, a). It is most common early in recall (recall_idx 1-2 hold 65% of mass), often when s was the first original token and is fed back at step L+1. The next outputs tend to be consonants such as l, f, d, r, c (out_tok l/s/f, next_out f at 18x lift). It never fires in the original phase and essentially never at the delimiter. It is extremely sparse, though: it fires on only 0.6% of copy-phase s inputs, and I could not find which context picks those out. Restricting by output/next-output tokens or by the absence of vowels/digits raised precision to at most ~7% while losing most recall. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.20), with the largest values on s fed back at recall_idx 1-2.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=l (+4.56), phase=2 & in_tok=s (+3.93), phase=2 & out_tok=l (+3.79), out_tok=s (+3.39), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+2.97), phase=2 & out_tok=n (+2.94). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.05), next_out=- (-1.14), n_digits=2 (-0.79).
